stories.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
stories.reason: Microsoft's 'Lazarus' shows an AI model can be backdoored by editing <10 rarely-used neurons, no retraining or fine-tuning data needed; concrete repro and a weight-comparison detector with real precision/recall numbers. Exactly the model-supply-chain-compromise angle Mine always-surfaces, with a working PoC.
key_facts: Microsoft's 'Lazarus' backdoors a model by editing fewer than 10 rarely-firing neurons, no retraining needed
Nemotron-Terminal-8B: 7 of >12,000 last-layer neurons edited, trigger command appeared in >=98.8% of triggered sessions, 0% of clean sessions
Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT: 51-99.5% success depending on setup; Qwen needed only 6 neurons
Terminal-Bench pass rate fell 46.59% -> 42.05% on the backdoored model; AIME math scores mostly preserved
A weight-comparison detector flagged 91.4% of edited checkpoints with 9.7% false positives (small test set: 35 edited/31 clean)
Asking Claude Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra to just inspect checkpoints performed poorly as a detection method
Microsoft credits Claude Code (Opus 4.5) with helping find the core idea; mitigation is weight-level checkpoint diffing vs. base model

stories.title: Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords
stories.reason: 35,578 publicly-open Grok-built apps found, ~1 in 10 leaking real internal data (hospital employee lists, ICU briefing, plaintext passwords) from 30+ organizations including 6 Fortune 500s. Concrete numbers, real-world harm, and a textbook AI-vibe-coding security failure — exactly the shadow-IT risk this newsletter tracks.
key_facts: Claroc found 37,571 Grok-built apps; 35,578 open to anyone without login
~1 in 10 open apps contained internal business or personal data; ~2% rated high/critical severity
Affected: 24 apps built by X/xAI staff, plus 30 other orgs (26 with 1,000+ employees, 6 Fortune 500) across construction, energy, healthcare, defense
Exposed data included a hospital's 3,500+ employee directory, an ICU patient briefing, and a timesheet app storing plaintext passwords

Root causes: 'Anyone with the link' as the default share setting, guessable/searchable grok.me subdomains via passive DNS, and a broken Grok-generated membership check (new users auto-approved before the check ran)
ChatGPT's app builder defaulted to private in the same test, showing defaults vary sharply by vendor

stories.title: Tracking Anthropic-discovered vulnerabilities
stories.reason: VulnCheck's critical seven-month audit of Anthropic's Project Glasswing: AI-assisted vuln discovery at scale, but with a skeptical, numbers-first take on how much of it is actually useful. Verifiable, numeric, and distinct from the usual launch-day hype pieces.
key_facts: Anthropic's Project Glasswing (launched Apr 7) is attributed 442 CVEs, ~0.5% of 93,450 CVEs published this year
Only 2 of those 442 CVEs are known exploited in the wild
Glasswing's internal ledger lists 37,966 findings; only 7,349 are public and just 217 are fixed
Claimed true-positive rate rose from 90.8% to 94.2%, but duplicates/withdrawals are rising too
On curl: 19 of 34 published reports were judged not-vulnerabilities, 6 confirmed low severity, 9 still pending
Findings are model-generated with no human review before reaching maintainers, per Anthropic

stories.title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
stories.reason: An AI pentesting agent (AntiFox, built on the ARTEX framework) is now tied to real intrusions that reached production AWS secrets via Arctic Wolf's incident telemetry — not a lab demo, an actual attack chain. Matches the AI-red-teaming/offense-tooling line Mine is built around, with primary-source attribution caveats noted.
key_facts: AntiFox is an autonomous AI pentesting platform (planner/worker multi-agent), built on the ARTEX framework, 251 forks / 474 stars at time of writing
Arctic Wolf Labs ties intrusions to it: ASPX web shell via IIS worker process, then config/log harvesting and an attempted internal DB connection using a leaked credential
Separately, attackers with a valid AWS credential used IAM to probe dozens of services; most calls were AccessDenied, but a GetSecretValue against a production secret succeeded
Attribution is to infrastructure only: Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces were linked to the malicious activity, not a confirmed threat actor or the tool's developers

stories.title: Huawei releases MACaQ, its internal quantizer for local inference
stories.reason: Huawei's MACaQ quantization toolkit ships running code (Apache-2.0) with concrete perplexity/speed numbers across multiple backends (llama.cpp, vLLM, Diffusers) and model families. Running code beating a described idea — exactly what Mine weights highest for inference infra.
key_facts: MACaQ (Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization), Apache-2.0, 129 stars/6 forks on GitHub
Produces W4A4 or weight-only checkpoints, plus 2/3/4-bit GGUF for llama.cpp; backends: Diffusers, llama.cpp, vLLM, PyTorch
A 122B-parameter model quantized in 64 minutes using 32.5GB device memory
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MACaQ-R Q4_K_XL: 22.36GB, KL divergence 0.0134 to FP16 vs. 0.0157 for Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL at the same size
Qwen3.8-27B on vLLM: perplexity 2.8994 vs. 2.8463 BF16, with 2.33x prefill / 2.58x decode speedups

stories.title: Faster Retrieval for Better, More Efficient RAG
stories.reason: Apple ML's official research on learned routing/retrieval for MIPS search (ICML 2026 paper, 'amortized MIPS') with concrete, large speedups over standard FAISS-style centroid routing on a real-scale benchmark. Primary source, numeric, inference-infra relevant.
key_facts: Apple ML research, ICML 2026: 'Amortizing Maximum Inner Product Search with Learned Support Functions'
SupportNet: reaches 95% routing recall ~1.9x faster than centroid routing (1.74ms vs 3.36ms) on ~2.6M-passage Natural Questions
KeyNet: reaches 99% recall with up to ~8x less time (0.23ms vs 1.8ms raw) and up to ~11x fewer keys scanned for the same recall
No code/repo mentioned on the page; only links to the paper, FAISS, and the Natural Questions dataset

stories.title: BotPsy: On-Device Personal Assistant with a Sub-Billion-Parameter Agentic Language Model
stories.reason: BotPsy is a real sub-billion-parameter open-weight model release with a full benchmark suite against its base model and a larger sibling, exactly Mine's 'open-weight model release with published weights' plus 'how models are served' lane, with hard numbers.
key_facts: BotPsy: 0.8B params, Tether AI Research, built on Qwen3.5-0.8B for on-device function-calling/agentic tasks; open weights, Apache 2.0
Post-trained via SFT, on-policy distillation from three Qwen3.5-4B teachers, and two RL rounds; ships bf16/Q8/Q4 safetensors+GGUF
Tool-use benchmarks vs. Qwen3.5-0.8B base / Qwen3.5-2B-Think: BFCL v4 44.0/23.4/37.7, ACEBench 58.7/30.1/55.4, tau-bench 51.5/23.2/46.5, ToolSandbox 64.6/30.5/41.2
Uses ~3x fewer reasoning tokens than its base on GPQA Diamond (3,690 vs 11,563 tokens); unsafe-response rate 21% vs 36% for the base in automated red-teaming

stories.title: What objective is reasoning solving?
stories.reason: A genuinely novel conceptual framing of LLM reasoning as pathfinding/success-probability optimization, deriving known RL-training behaviors (why CoT grows longer, why extra thinking plateaus, reward hacking) from one lens. Essay, not a paper, so the bare-arxiv override doesn't apply; reasonable HN traction (149 pts) without being over-saturated.
key_facts: Argues reasoning models optimize success probability over the distribution of sampled chains-of-thought, not correctness of any single path
Shows the REINFORCE policy-gradient update with binary reward is equivalent to rejection-sampling fine-tuning on the model's own successful paths, scaled by success rate
Explains why CoT length grows under RL training (successful paths tend to be longer) and why extra 'thinking' helps then plateaus (trained-in habit, not inherent value)
Frames reward hacking as arising from both an imperfect verifier and a sampler finding shortcut regions, worsening with more RL scale
